decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: Who wins when a police officer directing traffic and the traffic signal disagree?
cards.back: A police officer directing traffic can overrule the traffic signals, and a driver must always obey law enforcement orders and directions.

cards.front: What follows stealing or damaging airport, traffic or railroad-crossing signs or equipment?
cards.back: Stealing or damaging airport, traffic or railroad-crossing signs or equipment brings court penalties.

cards.front: In what order are the lights on a vertical signal, and where is red on a horizontal one?
cards.back: On a vertical signal, red is always on top, yellow in the middle and green third, with any green arrow at the bottom; on a horizontal signal, red is always on the left.

cards.front: What must you do at a steady red light?
cards.back: At a red light, stop before the intersection or crosswalk and stay stopped until the light turns green.

cards.front: What does a steady yellow light require?
cards.back: At a steady yellow light, stop before entering the intersection or crosswalk unless you are too close to stop safely.

cards.front: What does a yellow arrow warn you about?
cards.back: A yellow arrow warns that the light is about to go from green to red, giving you time to stop safely.

cards.front: On a green light, whom must you still yield to, and what extra yield applies before a left turn?
cards.back: On a green light, go ahead but yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection, and before turning left yield to oncoming vehicles.

cards.front: What does a green arrow allow, alone or with a red light?
cards.back: A green arrow, alone or together with a red light, lets you go only in the direction the arrow points, while still yielding to pedestrians.

cards.front: What does pressing a pedestrian push button do to the signal?
cards.back: At signals with pedestrian push buttons, pressing the button soon changes the flow so the side street gets a longer green.

decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
cards.back: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with care.

cards.front: What does a flashing red light require?
cards.back: A flashing red light means stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

cards.front: How does a flashing yellow light differ from a flashing red light?
cards.back: A flashing yellow light only asks you to slow down and take care, but a flashing red light requires a full stop before going on when safe.

cards.front: How must you treat a signal with no working bulbs and no one directing traffic?
cards.back: A signal with no working bulbs and no one directing traffic must be treated as a four-way stop.

cards.front: What does a steady orange raised palm tell pedestrians?
cards.back: When pedestrians face a steady orange raised palm, they must not step off the curb, and anyone already in the crosswalk will have time to finish crossing.

cards.front: What may pedestrians do on a white walking figure or countdown, and what must turning drivers do?
cards.back: On a steady white walking figure or countdown, pedestrians may cross, and New Jersey law requires turning drivers to yield to them.

decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: What are the three categories of signs and what does each do?
cards.back: Signs fall into three categories: warning signs for hazards that are hard to see, guidance signs that identify routes and destinations, and regulatory signs that control speed and movement.

cards.front: What is the red octagon used for?
cards.back: A red octagon, with eight sides, is used only for STOP signs.

cards.front: Which sign uses the red triangle?
cards.back: A red triangle, with three sides, is used for YIELD signs.

cards.front: What does a yellow pennant mark?
cards.back: A yellow pennant, a three-sided shape, marks a no-passing zone warning.

cards.front: What does a yellow pentagon mark?
cards.back: A yellow pentagon, with five sides, marks a school sign.

cards.front: What does an orange diamond warn of?
cards.back: An orange diamond warns of construction and maintenance work.

cards.front: What do blue, brown and green rectangular signs each give?
cards.back: Blue rectangular signs give motorist services and information, brown ones point to public recreation and scenic areas, and green ones give direction guidance.
cards.memory_hook: blue services, brown recreation, green directions

cards.front: What do general warning signs look like?
cards.back: General warning signs are yellow diamonds with a black symbol or word message.

cards.front: Besides general warnings, what else is the yellow diamond used for?
cards.back: A yellow diamond is also used for roadway hazard and railroad crossing warning signs.

decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: When is an advisory speed sign posted with a curve or turn warning?
cards.back: When the safe speed on a curve or turn is lower than the posted limit, an advisory speed sign is posted with the warning sign.

cards.front: What colors may pedestrian and bicycle warning signs use, and what do they tell drivers?
cards.back: Pedestrian crossing and bicycle warning signs may be standard yellow or an optional yellow-green, and they tell drivers to share the road with and yield to pedestrians and cyclists.

cards.front: What do orange road work signs warn of, and what happens to fines in New Jersey work zones?
cards.back: Orange diamond road work signs warn of lane closings, lane shifts, flaggers, uneven pavement and detours, and in New Jersey all traffic fines double in work zones.

cards.front: Which signs are posted alongside orange work zone signs?
cards.back: Reduced speed limit signs are posted alongside orange work zone signs.

cards.front: How should you drive near road work?
cards.back: Near road work, control your following distance and reaction time, read and follow the signs, be ready to slow or stop, and watch for workers and moving machinery.

cards.front: How much authority does a flagger have?
cards.back: A flagger has the same authority as a regulatory sign, so a driver who disobeys one can be cited.

cards.front: What marks a slow-moving vehicle on a public highway?
cards.back: A fluorescent, reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle marks a slow-moving vehicle, such as farm or construction equipment on a public highway.

decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: What do regulatory signs usually look like?
cards.back: Regulatory signs are usually vertical rectangles with black wording and border on a white background.

cards.front: What does a YIELD sign look like?
cards.back: A YIELD sign is a white inverted triangle with red wording and a red border inside a white border band.

cards.front: What does a DO NOT ENTER sign look like?
cards.back: A DO NOT ENTER sign is a white square holding a red circle crossed by a horizontal white band, with the words in white above and below the band.

cards.front: What do green and red national truck signs mean?
cards.back: Green national truck signs mark routes and ramps where trucks are allowed, while red ones mark where trucks are prohibited or where designated routes end.

decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: Which signs mark a railroad crossing and warn that one is ahead?
cards.back: A white X marks a railroad crossing, and a round yellow sign is the advance warning that a railroad crossing is ahead.

cards.front: What does the crossbuck mean, and why must drivers always yield to trains?
cards.back: The crossbuck, a white X-shaped railroad sign with black lettering, means the same as a Yield sign, and drivers must always yield to trains because trains cannot swerve.

cards.front: What do flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean, and when may you go?
cards.back: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is coming, and you may go only after they stop flashing and every other active warning device shuts off.

cards.front: Which railroad warnings are passive and which are active?
cards.back: Pavement markings, signs and crossbucks are passive railroad warning devices, while flashing red lights, ringing bells and lowered gates are active warnings.

decks.domain: Driver safety appendix: traffic signals, pedestrian signals, sign shapes and colors, warning, work zone, guidance and regulatory signs, and road markings

cards.front: How much legal force do road markings carry?
cards.back: Road markings carry the same force of law as signs and traffic signals.

cards.front: What do yellow center lines separate, and what do white lines separate?
cards.back: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving the same way and mark road edges.

cards.front: What does a dashed line on your side of the center line mean, and a solid one?
cards.back: A dashed line on your side of the center line means you may pass when it is safe, and a solid line on your side means you may not pass.

cards.front: With a solid and a dashed yellow line side by side, when may you pass?
cards.back: With a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line side by side, pass only when the dashed line is on your side, and finish the pass before the dashes turn solid.

cards.front: What do double solid lines mean for passing?
cards.back: Double solid yellow and white lines prohibit passing, so never cross a solid yellow line to pass, stay in your lane and keep right when driving slowly.

cards.front: What do road arrows and white dashed lines tell drivers?
cards.back: Road arrows used with other signs show the direction a driver must take from that lane, and white dashed lines separate lanes on multi-lane highways.

cards.front: What do edge lines mark?
cards.back: Edge lines separate the shoulder from the travel lane and mark the edge of the highway, and yellow edge lines do the same job.

decks.domain: Traffic signals, signs and markings confusables and continuation details

cards.front: Where do you stop when there is no stop line, and where when there is one?
cards.back: Where no stop line is painted, stop before the crosswalk when a sign, signal or pedestrian requires you to stop, and where a white stop line exists, stop at it.

cards.front: What do white special pavement markings such as STOP AHEAD alert drivers to?
cards.back: White special pavement markings such as STOP AHEAD, SCHOOL and RXR alert drivers to special conditions ahead.

cards.front: What do white diamonds on signs or in a lane mark?
cards.back: White diamonds on signs or painted in the lane mark high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes reserved for certain vehicles or for vehicles carrying several riders, and posted signs give the operating hours.

cards.front: How does a speed bump differ from a speed hump?
cards.back: A speed bump is a low ridge across the street, while a speed hump is a longer, flatter version.

cards.front: What do rumble strips do, and do they damage the vehicle?
cards.back: Rumble strips vibrate the wheel and make noise to warn of a decision point ahead or wake a dozing driver; they do not damage the vehicle and usually come with a caution sign.

cards.front: What is a roundabout, and why are severe crashes greatly reduced?
cards.back: A roundabout is a one-way circular intersection around a center island, and because traffic enters and exits only by right turns, severe crashes are greatly reduced.

recap_hooks.text: An officer directing traffic overrules the signals, and you always obey law enforcement directions.
Red means stop and stay stopped, steady yellow means stop unless too close, and green still means yield.
Flashing yellow asks you to slow down with care, while flashing red demands a full stop first.
A dead signal with nobody directing traffic works like a four-way stop.
The octagon is only for STOP, the red triangle is YIELD, the pennant warns of no passing and the pentagon marks a school.
Orange diamonds mean construction, and yellow diamonds carry general warnings.
Orange work zone signs come with doubled fines in New Jersey, and a flagger has the authority of a regulatory sign.
An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle marks it as slow-moving.
Most regulatory signs are white rectangles with black wording, and the YIELD sign is a white upside-down triangle bordered in red.
The crossbuck means yield, because trains cannot swerve, and flashing crossing lights mean a train is coming.
Signs and markings are passive warnings, while lights, bells and gates are active ones.
Yellow lines split opposite directions and white lines split same-direction lanes.
Pass only with the dashed line on your side, and never across double solid lines.
Stop at the white stop line, or before the crosswalk when there is none.
Rumble strips warn without damage, and a roundabout is a one-way circle entered by right turns.
